title: Solar Irradiance Through the Day
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Irradiance and air temperature on one time axis, across seasons and latitudes, with the thermal lag measured as a horizontal offset rather than asserted.

learningObjectives: Compare irradiance curves across seasons, latitudes and cloud conditions.
Explain the lag between peak irradiance and peak air temperature.
prerequisites: Reading a chart with two y-axes

keyQuestions: Why is the hottest part of the day not noon?
Which delivers more energy over a day: a tall narrow curve or a low broad one?
Your sensor briefly reads above the clear-sky maximum. Is it broken?
commonMisconceptions: Expecting peak temperature at solar noon.
Assuming a higher peak always means more energy.
Treating cloud-edge over-readings as sensor errors.
assessmentOpportunities: Explains the thermal lag in terms of heat capacity rather than restating it.
Distinguishes peak irradiance from daily total insolation.
Recognises brief over-readings under cumulus as real rather than faulty.
